name: Brihuega & Palacio de Ibarra
story: In March 1937 Mussolini's Corpo Truppe Volontarie under General Roatta drove down the Zaragoza road towards Guadalajara to encircle Madrid from the north-east. Rain grounded its aircraft on muddy airfields while Republican planes flew from paved runways. At the Palacio de Ibarra, a country house south of Brihuega, the Italian anti-fascist Garibaldi Battalion of the XII International Brigade fought Italian Blackshirts on 13–14 March: Italians against Italians. On 18 March Republican divisions under Líster, Mera and others counter-attacked and retook Brihuega, routing the CTV. It was the Republic's most celebrated victory and a humiliation for Fascist Italy.
see: Brihuega's walled old town above the Tajuña; the ruins of the Palacio de Ibarra stand in fields a few km south-east (private land).
plan: View the Palacio de Ibarra from the track only. Trijueque and Torija, on the N-II, were also battle sites and lie 15–20 minutes away.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
Italian losses are variously given as 600–3,000 dead and 2,000–4,000 wounded; the Republic's propaganda magnified the victory.
